record.paper_title: Open problems for tractability of multivariate integration
record.original_question: For integration of infinitely differentiable real functions on [0,1]^d whose partial derivatives are all bounded by one, is the number of function values needed for relative error epsilon not bounded by any polynomial in d and epsilon^{-1}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 1$ and consider the class
$$F_{d,\infty}=\{f\in C^{\infty}([0,1]^d):\ \|D^{\alpha}f\|_{\infty}\le 1\ \text{for every multi-index }\alpha\in\mathbb{N}_0^d\},$$
i.e. real-valued infinitely differentiable functions on the unit cube all of whose partial derivatives (of every order) are bounded in absolute value by $1$. For $f\in F_{d,\infty}$ consider the integration problem $I_d(f)=\int_{[0,1]^d} f(x)\,dx$, approximated by deterministic algorithms that use $n$ function values
$$A_{n,d}(f)=\phi_n\bigl(f(x_1),\dots,f(x_n)\bigr),$$
with adaptively chosen sample points $x_i\in[0,1]^d$ and arbitrary (measurable) mapping $\phi_n$. Define the $n$-th minimal worst-case error
$$e(n,d)=\inf_{A_{n,d}}\ \sup_{f\in F_{d,\infty}}\ |I_d(f)-A_{n,d}(f)|,$$
noting that $e(0,d)\le 1$. For $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, let the information complexity for relative error $\varepsilon$ be
$$n(\varepsilon,d)=\min\{n\ge 0:\ e(n,d)\le \varepsilon\,e(0,d)\}.$$
The class $F_{d,\infty}$ is said to be polynomially tractable for integration if there exist constants $C,p,q\ge 0$ such that
$$n(\varepsilon,d)\le C\,d^{q}\,\varepsilon^{-p}\qquad\text{for all }d\in\mathbb{N},\ \varepsilon\in(0,1).$$
Decide whether $F_{d,\infty}$ is intractable in this sense; equivalently, prove or disprove that no such constants $C,p,q$ exist (i.e. $n(\varepsilon,d)$ cannot be bounded by any polynomial in $d$ and $\varepsilon^{-1}$).
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Hinrichs, Novak, Ullrich, and Woźniakowski (2014) established the curse of dimensionality for integration over classes of $C^\infty$ functions when the bounds on successive derivatives are sufficiently large, and weak tractability is known under bounded directional derivatives. However, the specific case where all partial derivatives are bounded by one (the class $F_{d,\infty}$) remains unresolved: even weak tractability is reported as an open problem, so polynomial tractability/intractability in this class is not settled in the literature retrieved.

status_evidence.title: The Curse of Dimensionality for Numerical Integration of Smooth Functions II
status_evidence.snippet: For infinitely many differentiable functions we prove the curse if the bounds on the successive derivatives are appropriately large.
status_evidence.claim: Curse of dimensionality is proved for C^infty integration only under sufficiently large derivative bounds, not for the unit-bound class F_{d,infty}.

status_evidence.title: Multivariate integration in C∞([0,1]^d) is not strongly tractable
status_evidence.snippet: Multivariate integration in C∞([0,1]^d) is not strongly tractable.
status_evidence.claim: Strong tractability is ruled out, but polynomial tractability/intractability of F_{d,infty} is not established.

status_evidence.title: Super-polynomial convergence and tractability of multivariate integration for infinitely times differentiable functions
status_evidence.snippet: super-polynomial convergence of the worst-case error in weighted spaces of infinitely differentiable functions
status_evidence.claim: Positive tractability results exist only for weighted variants, leaving the unweighted F_{d,infty} case open.
